name: Guarded Agentic Chatbot
subtitle: Production-Grade AI Assistant with Built-In Guardrails
description: A production agentic chatbot built on LangGraph, with prompt-injection defense built into the graph. A fast regex check catches obvious attacks before any model call happens, and a semantic LLM check catches the reworded ones, on both what the user sends and what the model sends back, so a bypass on the way in doesn't help if the reply is still off-policy on the way out.

Ships with two real deployment tiers: a full AWS-native setup on ECS, RDS, and ElastiCache that handles roughly 39,000 monthly active users on real load-test numbers, and a budget single-server tier on Terraform and Ansible for $24 a month. Same design, same guardrails, sized to what the client actually needs.
technologies: LangGraph: Agent orchestration and guardrail graph
AWS Bedrock / OpenAI / Gemini / Ollama: Swappable LLM providers
Terraform: Infrastructure as code for both deployment tiers
PostgreSQL + pgvector: Vector store for retrieval
Docker: Local dev and both production tiers
roles: Designed and built the LangGraph agent graph, including the two-layer input/output guardrail system.
Architected both production deployment tiers and wrote the full Terraform infrastructure for each.
Ran and documented real load testing to establish the actual concurrent-user ceiling for both tiers.
Built the multi-provider LLM abstraction so the same graph runs on Bedrock, OpenAI, Gemini, or Ollama.

caseStudy.hook: Guardrails used for real load, at a price that scales with the your budget.
caseStudy.problem: An AI assistant that's actually production-ready has to be cost-effective to run and secure against attacks, including the reworded prompts that slip past a simple filter.
caseStudy.built: A two-layer guardrail graph on LangGraph: a fast regex check catches the obvious attacks before any model call happens, and a semantic LLM check catches the reworded ones, checking both what the user sends and what the model replies with, so a bypass on the way in doesn't help if the reply is still off-policy on the way out.
caseStudy.result: Same design, same guardrails, deployed at two different budgets depending on what the client needs.

name: BeemBridge
subtitle: File Transfer Without Walls
description: AirDrop is Apple-only. Quick Share skips iOS and macOS entirely. Beembridge works across all major platforms. Install it once on any device and it transfers to every other device running Beembridge, regardless of operating system.

Transfers work on your local network and online. Online transfers are peer-to-peer, so file data never passes through a server. Recipients can also receive files through a browser without installing anything.
technologies: Rust: Desktop application and core networking layer
roles: Built the full-stack desktop and mobile application, from UI to core networking logic.
Implemented cross-network P2P using STUN-based device discovery and WebRTC for the browser transfer mode.
Designed and managed the cloud infrastructure and CI/CD deployment pipeline.
Architected the product split between the open-source local app and the closed-source online platform.

caseStudy.hook: Works identically across every major platform, and no server ever sees your files.
caseStudy.problem: AirDrop only works between Apple devices, and Quick Share skips iOS and macOS entirely. Nothing lets you send a file to any device, on any platform, without installing extra software or routing it through someone else's server.
caseStudy.built: A cross-platform transfer app in Rust that works the same way everywhere: install it once and it finds every other device running it, on the same network or over the internet. Online transfers go peer-to-peer over WebRTC, so file data never touches a server, and recipients without the app can still receive files straight through a browser.
caseStudy.result: Works the same way on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android, with no server ever touching the file data in an online transfer.
